From: Buddy Williams Subject: state-recovery apply cannot converge on an active fleet �� nodes.json-only first_pass conflict fences a node indefinitely Body: Subject: state-recovery apply cannot converge on an active fleet �� nodes.json-only first_pass conflict fences a node indefinitely Refine version: 4.2.0 (linux_cli_web) Summary A node (bo2lnxnevo03-buddy) is stale-fenced from authoritative state sync by a first_pass conflict whose only unresolved path is nodes.json. The CLI/UI surfaces it as: "State sync is stale since . All-node counts are local and non-authoritative." The fence has persisted for hours (recurring conflict reports at 09:00Z, 09:30Z, 11:58Z, 12:07Z on 2026-08-17), does not self-heal, and the documented recovery cannot be applied while the fleet is live. Why this is a bug, not operator error 1. No real divergence. Every conflict report has local_state_head == remote_state_head (e.g. 8220fa6f��, later 7e66f885��). No Goal/Round/work state diverged �� the Git state histories are identical. The only difference is inside nodes.json (path_counts: differing=14, equal=1078), i.e. per-node heartbeat/health metadata. 2. nodes.json is written continuously by every node. Each node stamps its heartbeat into nodes.json every few seconds, so on a multi-node fleet the file always differs between snapshots. Treating that whole-file difference as an unresolved first_pass conflict fences a node essentially permanently, purely on heartbeat churn. 3. The recovery is un-appliable on a live fleet (TOCTOU). refine project state-recovery apply --authority live --preview-file

requires the reviewed preview to still match BOTH the current local and remote snapshots, but nodes.json changes on both sides between preview and apply: - remote side �� other nodes push heartbeats: "remote refine/state head changed" - local side �� this node's own heartbeat: "live state snapshot changed" - plus "newer conflict report replaced the reviewed report" and "Repository Git operations are busy" from the daemon's own fetch/publish cycle. ~135 back-to-back preview��apply attempts (workflow both running and paused) never landed once; refine project sync fails with the same project_sync_failed first_pass conflict. There is no --force/--allow-remote-advance flag, and pausing the local workflow does not stop the remote fleet's heartbeat pushes. Net: an operator on the fenced node alone cannot clear it without quiescing the entire fleet. Impact Degraded cross-node visibility on the fenced node (all-node counts become local/non-authoritative). Active Goal execution continues, so it is not a work stoppage, but the node's fleet view is wrong and the alarming warning recurs indefinitely. Requested fix (any one resolves it; A preferred) - A. Never fence on a heartbeat-only divergence. When local_state_head == remote_state_head, do not raise a first_pass conflict for nodes.json; merge it per-node-id with each node authoritative for its own record (last-writer-wins per record, union of records). - B. If A is infeasible, make recovery apply survive concurrent churn: scope compare/apply to just the reported conflict paths with a compare-and-swap retry, exclude the operator's own live heartbeat from the compared snapshot, and/or add --allow-remote-advance. - C. Don't downgrade cross-node counts to "non-authoritative" for a divergence that is heartbeat-only (state heads equal). Reproduction 1. Run a fleet of ��2 nodes actively heartbeating into nodes.json. 2. Induce/wait for a first_pass sync where the only unresolved path is nodes.json while local_state_head == remote_state_head. 3. refine project state-recovery preview, then refine project state-recovery apply --authority live --preview-file

�� rejected by remote-head/live-snapshot movement on every attempt. 4. refine project sync �� project_sync_failed first_pass on nodes.json. Evidence - Conflict reports: run/8082/state-sync-conflicts/latest.json (unresolved_paths: ["nodes.json"], matching heads). - refine project doctor: daemon reachable, git worktree clean, providers OK �� the fence is the sole failing subsystem. - Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.

result.summary: The plan safely covers semantic node-registry convergence across both sync phases, fail-closed conflict boundaries, concurrency tests, and affected intent documentation.

checklist.description: Add a cohesive node-registry merge module beside the existing Goal merge that parses base, local, and remote snapshots through NodeRegistry, requires unique nonempty canonical node identities and comparable update timestamps, retains the union of records, preserves one-sided changes, chooses the later version of a concurrently changed record, and declines ambiguous ties or invalid input.

Extend the existing semantic reconciliation boundary to prepare nodes.json and Goal results before generic conflict detection in both the initial pass and rejected-push retry, then carry all prepared paths through the established commit, live hydration, concurrent-write preservation, and baseline flow.

Keep automatic resolution atomic and narrow by never inferring node deletion from an absent record, withholding every prepared merge when any unrelated path remains unresolved, and retaining complete conflict reporting for malformed registries, duplicate identities, timestamp ambiguity, or genuine shared-state divergence.

Add focused unit and multi-node synchronization regressions covering disjoint heartbeat updates, record union, one-sided record changes, later-timestamp selection, equal-timestamp disagreement, malformed or duplicate registries, mixed unresolved paths, and remote advancement during a rejected push.

Update the Target App and Fleet intent pages in their existing format to define nodes.json as semantically merged shared state whose heartbeat-only churn does not stale-fence sync health or downgrade fleet-count authority while ambiguous or genuine conflicts still fail closed.

result.summary: Make nodes.json a semantically reconciled per-node registry during ordinary Git state synchronization so independent heartbeat updates converge across active nodes while invalid or ambiguous registry changes and genuine shared-state conflicts remain fenced.

governance_precheck.message: The finalized plan can be executed without violating the Constitution, governance rules, or enabled guidance.

checklist.description: Introduce a focused Git-sync node-registry reconciler that parses each nodes.json through the existing NodeRegistry model, rejects malformed or duplicate canonical identities and unusable update timestamps, unions records by node id, and deterministically selects the owner-side latest record without inventing a parallel state model.

Route nodes.json conflicts through semantic reconciliation before generic path conflict detection on both the initial pass and rejected-push retries, combining its prepared output with existing Goal merges and carrying it through the established commit, live hydration, concurrent-write preservation, and baseline boundaries.

Keep automatic resolution narrow so matching-head heartbeat-only churn converges, union semantics never infer record deletion, and invalid or ambiguous registries plus unrelated unresolved paths still produce the existing complete conflict report without partially writing prepared merges.

Add focused node-registry merge and multi-node synchronization regression cases for disjoint heartbeat updates, record union, same-record last-writer selection, remote advancement during push, malformed or duplicate registries, and mixed genuine conflicts.

Update the affected Target App and Fleet intent pages to define nodes.json as semantically merged shared state and state that heartbeat-only registry churn no longer degrades sync health or fleet-count authority while genuine ambiguity remains fenced.

result.summary: Teach Git-backed state synchronization to merge concurrent nodes.json updates by node identity so heartbeat-only fleet churn converges automatically without weakening conflict fences for genuine or invalid state.
